subject: general
question: Neap (low) tides occur when:

options.text: the earth is centered between the sun and the moon
the sun, the moon and the earth from a right-angled triangle
the sun, the moon and the earth are in the same line
the sun, the moon and the earth form a circle

solution:
The correct answer is __**the sun, the moon and the earth from a right-angled triangle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Neap tides occur when the gravitational forces of the moon and the sun are perpendicular to each other in relation to the Earth.
 
• This configuration happens when the moon is in its first or last quarter phases.
 
• During neap tides, the difference between high and low tides is minimal.
 
• Neap tides occur twice a month, coinciding with the quarter moon phases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tides**

 
 
• Tides are the rise and fall of sea levels caused by the combined effects of the gravitational forces exerted by the Moon, the Sun, and the rotation of the Earth.
 
• There are two main types of tides: spring tides and neap tides.
 
 
 
• **Spring Tides**
 
 
• Spring tides occur when the Earth, the sun, and the moon are in a straight line (during new moon and full moon).
 
• These tides have the highest high tides and the lowest low tides due to the combined gravitational pull of the sun and the moon.
 
 
 
• **Neap Tides**
 
 
• Neap tides occur when the gravitational forces of the moon and the sun are perpendicular to each other.
 
• During neap tides, the difference between high and low tides is the least.
 
• They occur during the first and last quarter phases of the moon.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Forces**
 
 
• The gravitational force is a force that attracts any two objects with mass.
 
• In the context of tides, the gravitational pull of the moon has the most significant effect due to its proximity to the Earth.
 
• The sun also affects tides, but to a lesser extent compared to the moon due to its greater distance from the Earth.
